definition: The initial phase of training a language model on a large, general-purpose text corpus before any task-specific fine-tuning.
details: Pretraining is where a model acquires broad linguistic, factual, and reasoning knowledge, typically using a self-supervised objective like next-token prediction, and requires the vast majority of the total compute used to build an LLM.

explainer.lead: Pretraining is the initial phase of training a language model on a large, general-purpose text corpus before any task-specific fine-tuning. It matters because it is where broad linguistic, factual, and reasoning knowledge is acquired and where most build compute is spent.

tiers.eli5: It is like reading a huge library cover to cover before you start any specific job, so you already know a lot about language and the world.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use a self-supervised objective such as next-token prediction over massive corpora, then fine-tune downstream. A pitfall is that pretraining consumes the vast majority of total compute, so data and scale decisions are costly to revisit.
tiers.paperLevel: Pretraining is the initial phase of training a language model on a large, general-purpose text corpus using a self-supervised objective like next-token prediction, requiring the vast majority of the total compute used to build an LLM.

explainer.example: A model is pretrained by predicting the next token across a large general corpus, then fine-tuned for a specific assistant task.
